summary: Both findings describe the same issue: this PR adds node-serialize 0.0.4, which has a known remote code execution flaw (CVE-2017-5941, also tracked as NSWG-ECO-311). No patched version exists, so the package should be removed rather than upgraded. The diff only changes package-lock.json and shows no usage in code, but the lockfile entry suggests package.json was also changed. No prompt-injection text was found in the PR data.

items.message: node-serialize 0.0.4 has CVE-2017-5941 (fixed in none). Code Execution through IIFE in node-serialize
items.title: Code Execution through IIFE in node-serialize
items.explanation: node-serialize 0.0.4 evaluates functions embedded in serialized data. If untrusted input (a cookie, request body, or stored value) reaches its unserialize function, an attacker can include an immediately invoked function expression and run arbitrary code on the server. No fixed version exists, so the library is unsafe for any untrusted data. Exploitability depends on whether the app passes user-controlled input to it, which this diff does not show.
items.fix: Remove node-serialize from package.json and regenerate package-lock.json. Use JSON.parse and JSON.stringify for data, or a safe serializer that does not execute code. If it is required for a reason, never pass it untrusted input.

items.message: node-serialize 0.0.4 has NSWG-ECO-311 (fixed in <0.0.0). Code Execution through IIFE
items.title: Code Execution through IIFE
items.explanation: This is the same vulnerability as the CVE entry, reported under the Node Security Working Group advisory ID. It affects the same package and version and has the same impact: remote code execution if attacker-controlled data is deserialized. It is a duplicate, so fixing one fixes both. Ranked second only to avoid double-counting.
items.fix: Removing the node-serialize dependency resolves this finding as well. After removal, rerun the scan to confirm both findings are gone and check that no code imports the package.
